label: Person
name: Rabindranath Tagore
summary:
Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) was a Bengali polymath—poet, novelist, musician, painter, and philosopher—who became the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913). His collection 'Gitanjali' (Song Offerings), which he translated into English prose, captivated W.B. Yeats and the Swedish Academy with its spiritual lyricism.

Born into the prominent Tagore family in Calcutta, he wrote his first poem at age eight and published prolifically in Bengali for six decades: over 2,200 songs (many now the national anthems of both India and Bangladesh), 50 collections of poetry, 13 novels, and hundreds of short stories. He composed the music for all his songs himself.

Tagore founded Visva-Bharati University at Santiniketan in 1921 as an experiment in open-air education that merged Eastern and Western learning traditions. He was knighted by the British in 1915 but renounced the honor in 1919 following the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, writing to the Viceroy: 'The time has come when badges of honour make our shame glaring.'

His influence on Bengali culture is immeasurable—he reshaped its literature, music, and visual arts. Einstein visited him in 1930 for their famous dialogue on the nature of reality. Tagore remains the only person whose compositions serve as the national anthem of two sovereign nations.
